description: Where a satellite is now, or at a given time: the point on Earth straight below it (latDeg, lonDeg, not where it is in your sky), its altitude, and whether it is sunlit, with url (its page on seeksat.com). A location is optional: it only sets the time zone for local times and for reading a time with no offset (UTC without one). A time more than 30 days from the orbital elements' epoch is refused. For where it is in your sky (azimuth and elevation) use find_satellites_up_now; for when it passes over use find_passes or find_next_visible_pass; for its orbit and TLE use get_satellite.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), all read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap. Prefer lat and lon, or a grid square, when you have them: a place name is a network lookup. Optional here.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

passTime.description: old name for time; still accepted.

satellite.description: NORAD catalog number (as a number or a string) or a name, e.g. 25544, "25544" or "iss".

time.description: when. Default: now. ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00:00-06:00"; a time with no offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00", is read in the observer's time zone, and the result echoes how it was read (interpretedAs). A local time the clocks skip at a daylight-saving change is moved forward, with a note.

name: get_position
title: Satellite position
